top_choice_rationale: P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) credits dated, identifiable steps: Calvo's tractable pricing device, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's welfare-based synthesis. Together they underpin how monetary non-neutrality and rule-based policy are analysed in research and in practice, and the framework has been extended for four decades without losing its core. I would word the citation around the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules, not the empirical performance of the simple model after 2008 or 2021-23. The costs are real: any trio omits Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, the credited work spans several decades and three kinds of contribution, and micro evidence on time-dependent pricing is mixed. P001 (Helpman, Melitz) is a close second. It has the cleaner credit set and more direct microdata testing of the selection and reallocation mechanism, and I would not call it a mistake as first choice if attribution and direct testing are weighted above breadth and durability of influence. The Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum question remains open for it. P004 follows because it has the cleanest attribution but thinner direct identification and some overlap with the 2022 prize. P003 follows because its identification is strong but the discovery boundary and the persistence of the estimates are contested. No award ranks last because several mature, well-defined contributions are available.
recusal_note: Co-author and IIES colleague of Per Krusell (secretary), who also supports P002; co-author with Timo Boppart (epidemiological-economic paper) and Richard Friberg (menu-costs paper), both of whom support P001. Krusell's agreement is not treated as independent evidence. No tie to the credited names on B015, B038, B050 or B036 is apparent from the profile. The 2018 Scientific Background cites my own climate work, but this is not relevant to any proposal here. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
